paragraphs.text: DSH 插件：在右侧栏查看外部子代理任务（Claude Code / Codex / ACP）的委派提示词、运行上下文与返回结果 / Inspect delegation context and ou
tcomes of external subagent tasks
# External Task Context (dsh-external-task-context)
Inspect the delegation prompt, runtime context, and returned outcome of external subagent tasks (Cla
ude Code, Codex, ACP) in a dedicated conversation view tab of the DSH Web app.
## Features and location
- **Conversation view tab**: the plugin registers the `external-task` entry in the session header's
View tab row (`Conversation / Traces / Context / Orchestration / Statistics / …`, labeled "External
tasks"). Selecting it renders the plugin inside the session body; there is no global panel or header

button.
- **Toolbar**: shows the active task's status, tool, and start time. When more than one tas
k exists, a task selector switches between them; the newest task is selected by default, an explicit
selection is kept while it exists, and a task that disappears falls back to the newest. Two chips,

`Conversation / Statistics`, switch the body.
- **Conversation**: one streamed, Markdown-rendered co
nversation. The delegation prompt is the right-aligned user bubble (with a metadata line above it) i
n a fixed 240px-high box that scrolls internally for long prompts. For Claude Code tasks, the live D
SH run log is appended below it while the task executes, and the returned content or settlement summ

ary is appended last once the task settles.
- **Log blocks**: assistant prose renders open; thinking
, tool calls, and tool results are collapsed by default and expand on click. Write/Edit-style calls
render a diff with removed lines red, added lines green, and muted context, limited to the changed h
unk plus two context lines; oversized hunks and long Write content show an explicit truncation marke

r. The log always reads the DSH trace only.
- **Statistics (Claude Code only)**: aggregate state, du
ration, message/tool-call/tool-result counts, last reported input/output tokens, and reported cost,
computed from the complete DSH log. While the task runs, the aggregates refresh every two seconds; a
manual refresh is always available.
## Data sources
Everything shown is already recorded in the **parent session log**; the plugin adds no session event
and changes no model-visible behavior:
1. `tool/call`: the delegation tool's argument JSON. `description` is the catalog label; `prompt` is
the delegated task; optional `cwd`, `provider`, `model`, `reasoning_effort`, and `agent_preset` are

the runtime context.
2. `subagent/catalog` v2 and v3: `{ version: 2 | 3, childId, childCreatedAt, m
ode: 'external', label? }`, which establishes the stable child id. Version 3 adds a required `name`

field; it is currently ignored, so the UI is unchanged.
3. A later `user/message` with `source.kind
=== 'subagent-settled'`: `source.summary` states how it ended; the text blocks are the summary line,
`Its closing message:` or `It left no closing message.`, the child's final text, an optional `Struc
tured result: ...`, and an optional diagnostic.
The host folds those events into the `externalTaskContexts` projection; the client only reads that p
olds those events into the `externalTaskContexts` projection; the client only reads that projection.
## Run logs (Claude Code only)
While a Claude Code task runs, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code` writes its execution log at `
<DSH_HOME>/logs/subagent-claude-code/<runId>.jsonl` — one JSON record per line: `start`, every raw S
DK message, then `end`. `runId` is the task's catalog `childId`.
The plugin reads it through its authenticated Fetch route `GET /api/external-task-context/log?childI
d=…&source=dsh&offset=…`, which returns only complete newline-terminated UTF-8 lines so the viewer c
an tail a growing file. The client polls once a second while the task is pending and stops when it s
ettles. Claude Code's native transcript is not fetched or shown.
Logs are written with mode `0600` in a `0700` directory and are pruned after 7 days by default. Olde
r tasks recorded before this feature have no log.
## Known limitations
External providers (Claude Code, Codex, ACP) run out of process; DSH does not persist their internal
steps or tool-call records. Run logs are implemented for the Claude Code provider only; Codex and A
CP tasks show the delegation context and returned outcome without a live log.
Also:
- Label matching is done only when unambiguous: the earliest unpaired call with the same catalog lab
el wins; without a label match, a single unpaired call is used; with several candidates the prompt a

nd options stay absent rather than guessed.
- Only the newest 20 unpaired delegation calls are retai

ned.
- Fork-inherited events (`seq < inheritedEventCount`) are not attributed to the current session

ed.
- Fork-inherited events (`seq < inheritedEventCount`) are not attributed to the current session.
## Installation
Requires DSH `0.2.2-rc.1` or newer and Node `^22.19 || >=24`. Live run logs need a provider with run
-log support: the official `0.2.2-rc.1` enables it through the patch package in `patch/`; master bui
he official `0.2.2-rc.1` enables it through the patch package in `patch/`; master builds include it.

The local build produces `lib/index.js` (host) and `lib/client.js` (web client).
Then enable the bundle in that profile. Restart the app or reopen the session so the host projection
and client bundle load.
## Official release
The official DSH `0.2.2-rc.1` provider does not write run logs, so live logs and statistics are unav
ailable with the stock package. Install the patch package in `patch/` to rebuild the provider with r
e stock package. Install the patch package in `patch/` to rebuild the provider with run-log support:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It replaces only the provider's `lib/index.js` after backing it up, then requires a DSH restart. See
`patch/README.md` for `--source`, supported versions, and upgrade notes.
## Privacy
The projection is persisted with the session projection cache, so prompts and returned content are s
tored a second time outside the session log (the content already exists in the session log). Treat t
hem with the same sensitivity in shared environments or when exporting a session.
